one_liner: Rust SQL data warehouse over object storage; ~1.6x faster than DuckDB on ClickBench hot runs on 192-vCPU hardware.
what_it_does: Databend is a client/server analytical SQL warehouse. A stateless databend-query service does the compute, a separate Raft-based databend-meta service holds the catalog, and table data sits as immutable Parquet blocks on S3, Azure, GCS or a local filesystem. Clients talk to it over HTTP: ClickBench uses its ClickHouse-compatible HTTP endpoint on port 8124 and a streaming_load API on port 8000. There is also a Python-only embedded 'local mode' (databend-driver[local] or the `databend` package), but nothing like DuckDB's in-process C/C++ library.
how_it_is_fast: Fuse storage prunes before reading. A snapshot points to segments, segments point to Parquet blocks, and multi-level min/max statistics prune segments and then blocks; per-block bloom indexes (xor8 by default, binary fuse32 as an option, from the xorf crate) skip blocks on equality predicates, and CLUSTER BY keys keep data sorted so range filters touch few blocks. Execution is a multi-threaded processor-graph pipeline (processors signal NeedData, NeedConsume, Sync or Async events to an executor), with GROUP BY and joins on a linear-probing hash table ported from ClickHouse's C++ implementation. On ClickBench the biggest gaps over DuckDB (5-9x on Q20-Q22 and Q28, 3-5x on the ORDER BY ... LIMIT queries Q24-Q27) are on point-lookup, LIKE and top-N queries, which fits pruning; that link is my inference. The heavy GROUP BY queries are close to even.
when_to_use: You want a shared, multi-user SQL warehouse over S3/GCS/Azure, with storage separate from compute, rather than an in-process library.
Repeated (hot) analytic queries on very large machines: ClickBench hot totals beat DuckDB ~1.6x on c7a.metal-48xl (192 vCPU) and c6a.metal.
Selective queries on large fact tables: point lookups on high-cardinality columns (bloom index), tenant/date range filters that match a CLUSTER BY key, and top-N ORDER BY ... LIMIT.
You need concurrent query serving from one process: ClickBench's concurrent test recorded 11.99 QPS over 10 connections with 0 errors (DuckDB's CLI entry skips this test).
You want Snowflake-style features self-hosted: snapshot-based time travel, stages/COPY loading, and external Parquet/ORC/Iceberg/Paimon tables (the repo has storage crates for each).
when_not_to_use: Mid-size machines: on c6a.4xlarge (16 vCPU) Databend's hot total is 41.93s vs DuckDB's 26.25s, and 9 queries are more than 1.5x slower (for example the REGEXP_REPLACE query Q29: 11.9s vs 6.5s).
Cold or first-touch queries: DuckDB wins the cold-run sums on every machine checked (162.8s vs 184.9s on c7a.metal-48xl, 115.2s vs 182.7s on c6a.4xlarge).
Embedded analytics inside a C/C++/Rust app or notebook where DuckDB's library and extension ecosystem is the point. Databend only embeds via Python, and the full product needs two daemons.

Joins or NOT IN subqueries that spill under memory pressure. Open bugs as of Sept 2026: #20512 (a spilling hash join fails once max_hash_join_spill_level >= 2), #20511 (NOT IN returns rows when a NULL is present and the mark join spills) and #20568 (duplicate rows from predicate pushdown into a RIGHT JOIN anti-join). There are 45 open C-bug issues.

You need everything under an OSI license: VACUUM, streams, materialized views, data masking, row access policies, storage encryption, attach table and workload groups are enterprise features that need a license key and fall under the Elastic-2.0 code paths.

integration.form: server binaries (databend-query + databend-meta) as tarballs, .deb packages or a Docker image; Python wheel for embedded local mode
integration.dependencies: At runtime, the databend-meta service plus object storage (S3/Azure/GCS) or a local fs. Building from source needs nightly Rust, build-essential, OpenSSL, protobuf, clang/LLVM and Python 3 (scripts/setup/dev_setup.sh).
integration.min_toolchain: Rust nightly (rust-toolchain.toml pins nightly-2026-08-28); local mode needs Python 3.12 or 3.13 with databend-driver >= 0.34.0
integration.platforms: Linux x86-64 and aarch64 (gnu tarballs and .deb in v1.2.948-nightly). The README badge says Linux, macOS and ARM, but no macOS binaries are among the release assets.
integration.thread_safety: Multi-session server that runs concurrent queries (ClickBench: 11.99 QPS at 10 connections, 0% errors on c7a.metal-48xl). Thread safety of the Python local mode is not documented.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: false — different deployment model (a client/server HTTP service instead of DuckDB's in-process library), a different SQL dialect, and data must be loaded into Fuse tables or read from stages/external files

gotchas: The ClickBench result comes from v0.9.53-nightly (Feb 2023), which ClickBench's install script pins. Current v1.2.9xx builds are not in that comparison, so today's numbers could be higher or lower.

The benchmark setups differ. Databend is a long-lived server that keeps its in-process caches between the 3 tries, and its hits table is CLUSTER BY (CounterID, EventDate, UserID, EventTime, WatchID). DuckDB's entry starts a fresh `duckdb hits.db` process for every try (BENCH_RESTARTABLE=no), so its hot runs only get a warm OS page cache, and its table has no sort key. Against that, Databend's times include a curl HTTP round-trip.
Releases are almost all -nightly tags (about daily). The last non-nightly release is v1.2.881 (2026-04-17), so pin exact versions.
Changing bloom_index_type with ALTER TABLE affects only new writes, so old and new filter types coexist until the data is rewritten. binary_fuse32 is about 4x larger than xor8.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Apache DataFusion shows the same ~1.6x over DuckDB on ClickBench c7a.metal-48xl, but it is an embeddable Apache-2.0 Rust library for building an engine. Pick Databend when you want a finished multi-user warehouse on object storage with time travel. For in-app embedding, DataFusion or chDB fit better, and Doris or StarRocks are the MPP-warehouse alternatives whose catalogued evidence is against ClickHouse, not DuckDB.
verified_claims_summary: ClickBench runs 43 queries on the 100M-row hits table, both engines on the same AWS c7a.metal-48xl (AMD EPYC 9R14, 192 vCPU). Databend v0.9.53-nightly (a prebuilt musl binary from Feb 2023, run 2026-09-26) sums best-of-3 per query to 9.91s, against 15.70s for the official prebuilt DuckDB CLI on its native .db file (run 2026-05-11, version not recorded): ~1.6x, faster on 35/43 queries, ~1.75x geomean using ClickBench's +10ms shift. c6a.metal looks similar (10.65s vs 17.32s), but c6a.4xlarge reverses (41.93s vs 26.25s), cold sums favour DuckDB everywhere, and neither side states compiler or flags.
status_note: Actively developed (default-branch commits daily, last push 2026-09-26, 9.45k stars) but shipped almost entirely as nightlies, and an Apache-2.0 core with Elastic-2.0 enterprise directories makes usability 'mixed'.
